record_notes.DCP-LETT-1817: January 8, original header 1855 editorially corrected to 1856; all seventeen body blocks, sixty-eight footnotes, full long thirteen-section Notes for Mr Darwin enclosure, separate annotations and bibliography read. Corrected year supported by sequence and contents, not an arrival timestamp. Answers missing November 5 and 22 Darwin letters; Moore queries said to be separately forwarded are not preserved. Orang paper unavailable for this mail, lion paper available and ass paper referred to London publisher: these are different transmission states. P3 corrects misunderstanding: interbreeding within Coracias and within Treron, not between those genera. Railway anecdote source recalled uncertainly, camel parentage is reported and not automatically proved by one-humped appearance. Indian donkey stripes expressly not zebra intermixture. P8 onward are substantive postscripts after signature, including regional intergradation, species-versus-race uncertainty, isolated Mydaus populations and speculative cabbage origin. Historical racial and ethnographic assertions remain Blyth claims. Full enclosure contains nested quotations, guinea-fowl historical-origin arguments, contradictory flight observations, possible hare/grouse varieties, suspected pheasant relations, cattle notice and Crump forwarding lead, revised Turkey-name etymology and poultry-source inquiries. Two physically attached feathers described in footnote 44 are not pictured in current HTML; their markings are not independently visually verified. Later Origin/Variation/Natural selection citations and Darwin marginal abstracts do not date contemporary knowledge. Docket 10 is sequence numbering, not receipt. Enclosure is present in this HTML despite historical separate1818 label; do not count it twice. Separate Crump1819 is being recovered additively, not claimed read here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1825: January 23, 1856 exact Calcutta ALS; seven full blocks, thirty-one footnotes, annotations, bibliography and actual spur drawing read. Home letters arrived about midnight last night, including an undated Darwin letter whose postscript acknowledged October 8 and 22 Blyth letters. This provides indirect prior knowledge evidence but no surviving Darwin reply text or exact Darwin receipt day. Echo du monde savant known only through a cited review, not directly read by Blyth. Goldfish origin is a hypothesis; article and jungle-fowl skins are promised, not Darwin receipts. Blyth proposes five distinct gallinaceous families and corrects turkey tuft to feathers, while muscular foundation was news from Darwin. Live wild dog personally seen yesterday; putative later London transfer is prospective. Seychelles conspectus unknown, sources and specimens requested. P5 corrects numerous African fowls versus numerous races, and Rock Pigeons ambiguity; illustration shows extra spur arising beneath an existing spur, no scales or measurements. Bantam name versus biological origin and fallow-deer colour versus other variation kept distinct. Annotated number11 is not a delivery date. Bibliography Thomson1848 Lochaber entry does not match Allen and Thomson1848 Niger narrative cited in apparatus; do not use mismatched bibliography to replace source identity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1832: February 23, 1856 exact Calcutta ALS; five complete blocks, twenty-four footnotes, annotations, bibliography, raw half MathML and actual labelled Gallus head drawing read. Previous brief letter got to post office, not evidence it reached Darwin. Four printed appeal copies now sent versus rough proof sent previous mail; their exact identification as salary memorial is apparatus inference and eventual1864 pension is later. February20 anniversary walk is an actual prior event, proposed Calcutta gardens future. Gallus varius first living observation includes a pale bluish-lake comb, red/yellow throat regions and blue tip labelled in figure; hybrid Gallus oeneus claim remains Blyth report. Pigeon procurement and ten-pound proposal, macaw/marmoset barter and prices remain negotiations, not completed shipments. Complaint about Bartlett is Blyth allegation, no independent finding. P3 explicitly answers missing December16 Darwin letter, cannot recall exact authority for Oman asses or red-deer infertility. Wild dog is now dead with skin/skeleton preparation ongoing; earlier identification revised after Hodgson examination. Canine-hybrid experiment advocates matched sibling controls, not completed comparative results. P4 half-bred Sonneratii is 1/2, not twelve birds; observed repeated infertile eggs qualified by possible individual fertility differences. Coracias skins procured by Blyth, not Darwin. Northern/southern bird comparisons and tropical gaps qualified; Darwin consultation note is undated. Docket12 is sequence marker only.
